final:
STATUS: pass

SUMMARY: I ran 19 probes covering the wrapper, the composition orders with Compress, Recoverer, ServeContent, FileServer, Flush/ResponseController, obs-text tags, `*` in lists, and concurrency. None reproduced a failing acceptance criterion. Two real deviations from the spec or RFC showed up as [minor], and the probe files are deleted.

FILES TOUCHED: none (scratch probes `middleware/zz_redteam_*_test.go` were created and removed; `git status` matches the start: M README.md, A etag.go, A etag_test.go)

FINDINGS:
- [minor] Compress inside ETag, `Compress(5,"text/plain")(ETag(h))`: the gzip and identity responses get the same ETag (`"532e12b8…"`). RFC 9110 §8.8.3 says a content-coded representation needs its own tag. Reproduced; the 304 to a gzip client using the identity tag is harmless. The tag is computed over the uncompressed body, so it is arguably within "derived from the body".
- [minor] GET with `Content-Length: 5` and no body gets no ETag (`etagServe` with declared length, GET → `ETag=""`). Criterion 2 wants an empty GET body to still get a tag. This is a handler that lies about its length, and `declaresUnwrittenBody` applies to GET as well as HEAD. Reproduced.
- [minor] Headers set after `WriteHeader(200)` are honored under ETag. On a real server with plain chi, `X-Late` is absent; with ETag it is `"1"`. net/http ignores it, so the behavior diverges. Reproduced.
- [minor] HEAD on `ETag(http.FileServer)` returns no ETag while GET does. This is what criterion 6 mandates (HEAD writes no body, so no computed tag), but clients that HEAD first will never see a tag. Reproduced; spec-compliant.
- [minor] `If-None-Match: *, "a"` returns 200. This is malformed per RFC (`*` must stand alone), so the no-match is defensible. Not reproduced as a bug.

CHECKS:
- `Compress(ETag)` and `ETag(Compress)`, gzip + If-None-Match → 304 with no Content-Encoding (pass)
- `Compress` streaming with Flush on real server → no ETag, body "onetwo", no CE (pass)
- Recoverer + ETag, panic after buffered write → 500 (pass)
- `ResponseController` SetWriteDeadline and Flush on real server → nil errors, no ETag after flush (pass)
- ServeContent: If-Modified-Since → 304 passthrough; Range → 206 "234" with no ETag (pass)
- FileServer GET/HEAD: GET ETag present, HEAD none (expected per criterion 6); 304 on GET match (pass)
- obs-text tag `"\xff\xe9"` matches `W/` form (pass)
- 32 concurrent real-server GETs with If-None-Match, `-race` → all 304 with same ETag (pass)
- Handler writes 304 explicitly → passes through with its tag (pass)
- WriteHeader(103) then body on real server → 200 "ok" (pass)
- Hijack/Push error text and Unwrap identity: covered by the existing tests; I read them and did not re-run them.

OPEN QUESTIONS: Should the orchestrator treat the Compress-inside-ETag shared tag (gzip vs identity) as a blocking RFC issue or accept it as "derived from the body"? And should GET with a declared-but-unwritten body get a tag, or stay as is?
